No commits on either file since 2026-08-21. Recommendation: keep — REVIEW-CRITICAL; brief v2.0.0 already corrects the inert lgtm[] premise, so work from the rewritten step 3.
evidence: Live re-verify at HEAD via `gh api /repos/falkcorp/audiobook-organizer/code-scanning/alerts?state=all` for rule go/request-forgery: #662 state=open, internal/metadata/cover.go:148 (line drifted from 137); #645 state=open, internal/covers/covers.go:82. Neither dismissed_reason set. Both nolint markers still present verbatim: cover.go:148 `//nolint:noctx // URL already validated above`, covers.go:82 `//nolint:gosec // URL is validated by caller`. Per the brief's own acceptance criteria, each alert must end EITHER fixed OR dismissed-via-API-and-read-back; neither has happened for either alert — no dismissal call was ever made (dismissed_reason is null on both) and no code changed the security posture. Code-level asymmetry confirmed by direct read: cover.go DOES have real protection — validateCoverURL (http/https allowlist, cover.go:66) + safeCoverDialContext (cover.go:76-96, resolves host then blocks IsPrivateIP for both IPv4 CIDRs and IPv6 ::1/128, fc00::/7, fe80::/10) wired into the Transport's DialContext, so it also re-applies on every redirect hop (same Transport is reused by net/http's default redirect handling) — this is plausibly sufficient for a dismissal. covers.go:82 by contrast only has `covers.IsAllowedCoverSource` (covers.go:37, a raw string-prefix allowlist of 4 known hostnames) feeding into `http.Get` (= http.DefaultClient, no custom DialContext, no CheckRedirect) — a redirect from an allowed host to 169.254.169.254 would be followed with zero IP-level check. That asymmetry means #645 genuinely needs a fix (DialContext-level IP block + redirect-safe transport), not just a dismissal; #662 is a dismissal candidate. Both outcomes are still undone at HEAD.
notes: ~100 PRs landed since 09-02 and neither alert was touched — the 09-02 verdict still holds at HEAD, re-verified independently rather than trusted. covers.go:82 (#645) is the more clearly actionable of the two: no per-connection IP validation and no CheckRedirect, unlike cover.go's site.
